subtopics.title: Why Atoms Bond — Valence Electrons and Lewis Diagrams

questions.question: Atoms form chemical bonds in order to:
options: Reach a full outer energy level — the stable arrangement of a noble gas

questions.question: A Lewis diagram shows the element's symbol surrounded by dots representing:
options: Only its valence electrons — the outer-level electrons that do the bonding

questions.question: The Lewis diagram of oxygen, in group 16, shows:
options: Six dots — two pairs and two singles, giving oxygen two bonding hooks

questions.question: Two non-metal atoms reach full outer levels by:
options: Transferring electrons from one to the other
Losing electrons into a shared pool

questions.question: In a water molecule, the oxygen atom:
options: Shares three pairs with one hydrogen
Shares one pair with each of two hydrogens, keeping two lone pairs
Transfers two electrons to the hydrogens

questions.question: The bond in the O two molecule is a:
options: Double bond — each oxygen needs two more electrons, so two pairs are shared

questions.question: Nitrogen gas is so unreactive in air because the N two molecule holds a:
options: Triple bond — three shared pairs, among the strongest bonds in chemistry

questions.question: In methane, C H four, carbon uses:
options: Two double bonds and two lone pairs
One bond and three lone pairs
Its four unpaired dots to form four single bonds with four hydrogens, leaving no lone pairs

subtopics.title: Ionic Bonding — Transfer and the Lattice

questions.question: The ionic bond in sodium chloride is the:
options: Shared pair between sodium and chlorine
Electrostatic attraction between the Na plus cation and the Cl minus anion after electron transfer

questions.question: Using periodic-table positions, the formula of calcium chloride is:
options: CaCl two — calcium's plus two needs two chloride minus ones to balance to zero

questions.question: NaCl is called a formula unit rather than a molecule because:
options: Ionic compounds form a giant crystal lattice, and the formula gives only the simplest ratio of ions
Salt molecules are too small to see
The name molecule is reserved for gases

questions.question: Ionic compounds conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved because:
options: Water is itself a good conductor
Only then are the charged ions free to move — in the solid lattice they are locked in place

questions.question: Metallic bonding is the attraction between:
options: Positive and negative ions in a lattice
A lattice of positive metal ions and the sea of delocalised electrons among them

questions.question: Metals bend where ionic crystals shatter because:
options: The electron sea flows around rearranged ions, so the bonding survives the shift
Metal atoms are softer than ions

questions.question: The relative formula mass of calcium chloride, CaCl two (Ca = 40; Cl = 35,5), is:
The relative molecular mass of carbon dioxide, CO two (C = 12; O = 16), is:

subtopics.title: Sharing the Data, Swapping the Chairs

questions.question: In the data-bundle picture, the shared bundle both friends count as theirs represents:
options: A shared electron pair — a covalent bond between two non-metals

questions.question: After sodium gives its chair — its electron — to chlorine, the ionic bond is:
options: The attraction between the resulting plus and minus badges — the opposite charges
A pair shared between the two

questions.question: To predict share versus swap, read the periodic table:
options: Two metals share; two non-metals swap
Two non-metals share (covalent); a metal and a non-metal swap (ionic)

subtopics.title: The Salt Grid and the Electron Sea

questions.question: Salt is hard to melt because melting the grid requires:
options: Breaking strong plus-minus attractions that run in every direction throughout the lattice

questions.question: Hitting a salt crystal shatters it because shifting a layer:
options: Forces like charges against each other, and the grid rips apart

questions.question: A copper wire conducts electricity because its delocalised electrons:
options: Belong to the whole metal and are free to drift, so charge flows when pushed

questions.question: The relative molecular mass of water, H two O (H = 1; O = 16), is:
options: 18 — two hydrogens at 1 each plus one oxygen at 16

questions.question: The reliable three-beat method for any formula mass is:
options: Inventory the atoms, multiply each count by its atomic mass, then add
Add all the atomic masses, then multiply by the number of elements
Round every mass to the nearest ten first
Divide the biggest mass by the smallest
